text: One invoice was matching thirty rows somewhere inside revenue_mart's own join. This lesson reads the real SQL, finds the exact line, and fixes it.
The join matched billing against active_members using a date range -- but active_members has one row per member per calendar day, so a thirty-day invoice matched thirty rows before the SUM ever ran.
Checking the matched-row count against each billing period's actual day count proves it: the multiplier tracks the calendar exactly. That's a grain mismatch, not a data-quality problem.

The fix joins billing against member_activity_mart instead, which is already one row per member per month. One invoice now matches exactly one row, and the total drops to match the hand-summed billing figure exactly.
A new test now guarantees this exact fanout can never silently come back. Next: formally reconciling every number before anyone outside the team has to trust it blind.
